summary: NAQsim is an open-source full-stack simulator for neutral-atom fault-tolerant architectures built on transversal gates. As a first use it identifies surface-code patch rotations as a hidden bottleneck and derives a near-rotation-free architecture (D3-ROT) that runs 2.27x faster with minimal footprint overhead.
motivation: Neutral-atom operations are orders of magnitude slower than on superconducting qubits, so architects need reliable tools to find fast FTQC designs.
method: A simulation framework spanning software, classical hardware and the quantum device is used for full-stack co-optimization of transversal surface-code architectures.
result: Eliminating most patch rotations gives a 2.27x speedup on practical FTQC benchmark workloads.
